To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chemical composition of the ash and slag obtained from the burning of the Romanian lignites is similar, and that they contain a significant amount of heavy metals and alkaline and alkaline-earth metals.

(1) the chemical composition of ash and slags obtained from lignite burning is similar; (2) the ash and slags contain high amounts of CaO, MgO, SiO2 and Al2O3; (3) the ashes and slags are rich in CaCO3 and MgCO3; (4) the ashes and slag contain a high amount of water; (5) the ash and slag can be used in different industries after the residual material is removed;

the chemical composition of the ashes and slags obtained from the burning of lignite is very similar to those obtained from the burning coal, and the main difference between the two types of ashes and slags lies in the higher content of sulfur in the ashes and slages obtained from lignite.
